function: Estimating the BD-RIS cascaded channel (its autocorrelation matrix) from user received-power measurements under varying training reflection patterns (pp. 1-3).
system: Single-antenna BS and user, group-connected reflecting BD-RIS with N=16 elements (4x4), group sizes 1, 2, 4, 8, narrowband block fading, frequency not stated (pp. 2, 4, 5).
method: Single-layer neural network whose weights are the channel, trained by backpropagation on the power measurements of each channel (supervised, cosine-annealed learning rate); greedy training-pattern selection (pp. 3-5).
data_channel: Custom simulation: Rayleigh BS-user channel, distance-based path losses for all links, BS-RIS and RIS-user fading unspecified, random user positions, 100 Monte Carlo runs; no dataset (pp. 4-5).
test_conditions: Same simulated setup for training and testing: each run trains on the power samples of one random channel; sweeps over sample number, noise power, group size (p. 5).
baselines: Only proposed greedy TRP selection versus random TRP selection, both with the same network (p. 5); no least-squares, tensor-decomposition, or other learned estimator simulated.
metrics: NMSE in dB of the estimated cascaded-channel autocorrelation matrix, averaged over 100 Monte Carlo runs (p. 5).
complexity: Stated order O(N0 N) for the single-layer network, without derivation; 2*N0*N+2 channel parameters to estimate (pp. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 4: "The BS-user channel follows Rayleigh fading" with distance-based path-loss formulas; custom simulator, no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 4: "for unseen data, as also demonstrated numerically in [10]." This claim cites earlier work; this letter's simulations (p. 5) only sweep sample number, noise power, and group size, with no test on a condition unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 5: "the proposed scheme and random TRP selection" is the only comparison, an ablation of the selection step with the same network; no non-learned estimator (LS [7], tensor [8]) or earlier learned estimator ([9], [10]) is simulated.
q4_support: p. 4: "It can be shown that the complexity order of the single-layer" NN architecture is O(N0 N); a single sentence with no derivation and no runtime.
q5_support: p. 4: "The BS-user channel follows Rayleigh fading"; channels are simulated, and no code or data link and no public dataset appear in the 6 pages.
notes: Borderline on no_learning: the network has the channel as its weights and is fitted by backpropagation to the power measurements of each realization, with no offline training across channels. It is kept because the paper presents it as a trained neural-network estimator, p. 4: "we can use backward propagation to iteratively update the NN weights"; the reviewer may confirm. Check 6 does not apply because the link has a BD-RIS although BS and user have one antenna each. The q4 mark rests on one sentence stating O(N0 N). The PDF is the arXiv v2 preprint (arXiv:2509.05639) and carries no DOI; it is identified by title and topic.
